title: How do we multiply four numbers by 11 in one line each?
description: Four numbers, from two digits to seven digits, are multiplied by eleven by adding each digit to the one on its right with carries. The longest one is checked by adding ten times the number to the number.
teaching_notes: One idea: times eleven adds each digit to its neighbour with carries. Same method as the times eleven video in your book.

video_script.why: The child has written times eleven in one line for a four digit number. Here the numbers get longer and the carries repeat.
video_script.substitution: Bring down the last digit, add each digit to the one on its right with carries, bring down the first digit, and check the longest one by adding.
video_script.anchor: four numbers each multiplied by eleven
video_script.payoff_line: Add each digit to its neighbour, and carry when needed

final_answer.spoken: one thousand thirty four, five thousand four hundred forty five, thirty six thousand sixty nine, and fifty two million seven hundred three thousand eight hundred sixteen

video_script.design: One idea: times eleven adds each digit to its neighbour with carries. Uses the method of the times eleven video. The longest number is checked by adding ten times the number to the number.

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, take ninety four, and bring down the four.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Nine plus four is thirteen, so write three and carry one.
<bookmark mark='c'/>The first nine plus the carried one makes ten.
The answer reads one thousand thirty four.

marks.b: 9 + 5 = 14 is written, with 4 written and 1 carried
marks.c: 4 + 9 + 1 = 14 is written, with 4 written and 1 carried

beats.colours: the carried digits in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, take four hundred ninety five, and bring down the five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Nine plus five is fourteen, so write four and carry one.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Four plus nine plus one is fourteen, so write four and carry one again.
<bookmark mark='d'/>The first four plus the carried one makes five.
The answer reads five thousand four hundred forty five.

marks.b: 7 + 9 = 16 is written, with 6 written and 1 carried

marks.d: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 is written, then 3 comes down, and 36069 is read off

beats.colours: the carried digits in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, take three thousand two hundred seventy nine, and bring down the nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Seven plus nine is sixteen, so write six and carry one.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Two plus seven plus one is ten, so write zero and carry one.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Three plus two plus one is six, and the first digit three comes down.
The answer reads thirty six thousand sixty nine.

marks.b: 5 + 6 = 11 and 2 + 5 + 1 = 8 are written with their digits and carry

beats.colours: the carried digits in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step four, take the seven digit number, and bring down the six.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Five plus six is eleven, so write one and carry one.
Two plus five plus one is eight, with no carry.
<bookmark mark='c'/>One plus two is three. Nine plus one is ten, so write zero and carry one.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Seven plus nine plus one is seventeen, so write seven and carry one.
Four plus seven plus one is twelve, so write two and carry one.
<bookmark mark='e'/>The first four plus the carried one makes five.

narration: <bookmark mark='ten'/>Step five, check the longest one by adding.
Ten times the number is forty seven million nine hundred twelve thousand five hundred sixty.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>Adding the number once more gives fifty two million seven hundred three thousand eight hundred sixteen.
That matches the digits we found.
